title: ADR Decision Record v1
description: One record per architecture decision, appended once to specs/ADRs/decisions.jsonl (v0.5.0 specs-canon closure, operator ruling 2026-08-28). A superseded decision stays in decisions.jsonl with `status: superseded`, named by its successor's `supersedes`; its id is never reused. `id` is monotonic and gap-free over the one file. Who accepts: specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md §2.

id.description: Zero-padded 4-digit sequence number, monotonic and gap-free over decisions.jsonl — never reused, never re-numbered.

ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp this record was appended.

status.description: proposed: open. accepted: requires a non-empty measured_by and a ruling. rejected: no consequence elsewhere. superseded: retired in place by the successor named in that successor's `supersedes`.

context.description: What forces make this decision necessary — the problem, not the solution.

decision.description: "We will …" — the choice, stated as a commitment, not a discussion.

measured_by.description: The existing mechanical check that proves this decision holds. Free text; required non-empty once `accepted`.

supersedes.description: Id (NNNN) of the record this one supersedes — or comma-separated ids, ascending, when one decision retires several — or null.

amends.description: Id (NNNN) of the record this one amends, or null.

ruling.description: The operator's ruling (ADR 0151): its date and his verbatim words or grill answer id; required on `accepted`.

allOf.description: The operator-only acceptance law, expressed MECHANICALLY (0.4.7 FR6): an 'accepted' record must carry a non-empty 'measured_by' — a decision nobody can measure is not a principle, it is prose. Stated in this schema rather than in a test's hand-rolled copy, so the one validator the ledgers doctor runs and the one the contract test runs are the same validator.

examples.title: Features depend on ports, not adapters
examples.context: Features need I/O (git, filesystem, subprocess) but must stay unit-testable without real I/O.
examples.decision: We will define a Protocol in core/protocols/ for every I/O boundary a feature needs, and inject a concrete infrastructure/ adapter at the composition root (container.py) — a feature module never imports infrastructure directly.
examples.consequences:
+ features are testable with fakes, no real I/O in unit tests
- one extra indirection layer per I/O boundary
